lines.text: Sunlight looks white, so why is the clear sky above you blue and not white too?
White sunlight carries all the colours of the rainbow, so why does the sky pick out the blue?
Each colour travels as a wave, and blue light travels in shorter waves than red light.
The air above you is full of gas molecules, and all that sunlight has to pass through them.
Gas molecules scatter blue light in all directions more than the other colours, so blue reaches you from the whole sky.
Near the horizon the sky looks paler, because that light crossed more air and its blue was scattered many times in many directions.
Send this to the next person who asks you why the sky is blue.
